subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should `clawhub skill publish` reject source-provenance flags, preserve them only as explicitly unverified public attribution, or gain a server-verified provenance flow?
rationale: The correct choice defines a public trust contract and determines whether new server verification, a separate attribution model, or only CLI/docs changes are appropriate; source inspection cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Reject unsupported skill source fields
options.body: Keep verified provenance exclusive to server-resolved GitHub imports and make `skill publish` fail with guidance to the supported package/import workflow.

options.title: Expose unverified attribution
options.body: Persist publisher-supplied repository details separately from trusted provenance and label them unverified in API and UI surfaces.

options.title: Build verified CLI provenance
options.body: Verify repository ownership, commit/path content, and uploaded artifact correspondence before writing trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Reject unsupported skill source fields
recommendation.body: Keep verified provenance exclusive to server-resolved GitHub imports and make `skill publish` fail with guidance to the supported package/import workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged GitHub-backed source-sync work is the clearest available ownership signal for the existing verified-provenance design.
